nodes.description: Inducible deletion of betaENaC in the adult nephron produces a severe PHA1-like phenotype with weight loss, hyperkalemia and dehydration but only minor salt wasting, rescued by a low-potassium diet.

Airway ENaC absorbs sodium and liquid from the airway surface. Patients with systemic PHA1 have no airway sodium absorption, more than double the normal airway surface liquid volume, and recurrent chest congestion, coughing and wheezing in early childhood. This was shown in cohorts with ENaC subunit mutations generally; betaENaC-null mice clear neonatal lung liquid almost normally, so how far the airway phenotype applies to the SCNN1B form specifically is not settled.

nodes.description: Biallelic frameshift, nonsense, splice-site or missense SCNN1B variants remove or impair the ENaC beta subunit. Truncated beta subunits can still support weak trafficking and assembly with alpha and gamma subunits, and the missense p.Gly37Ser variant lowers channel open probability, so most alleles drastically reduce rather than strictly abolish amiloride-sensitive sodium current.
